memory_candidates.content: A fence-interior heading-shaped line can corrupt a TASK PREMISE, not just a measurement. In skill-distill/SKILL.md, '## Auto Distill Complete' at line 1495 sits inside a ``` fenced output example; a boundary scan from it to EOF yields 43,254 B, and that number propagated unchallenged from the task description into a research report as 'an --auto-only output template, 46% of the file'. It is actually five unrelated sub-mode specifications (revise, meta, review, learn, dream) plus two shared sections; the real '### Sub-Mode: auto' is 3,358 B, below any extraction bar. Planner-side rule: when a task names a section by heading text and a byte size, verify the heading is NOT fence-interior (count ``` delimiters above it -- odd means inside) and that the file's real heading map at that level contains it, BEFORE planning an extraction around it. A fence-aware heading map is the cheapest check that distinguishes a real section from a display template.
